cases.scope_review: The compiled NonvacuumBrinkmannStencil result proves the exact five-point harmonic/radial readout and binds its source norm to the same recursively constructed midpoint matter record. The time-indexed extension proves that each natural-indexed history step supplies the exact rate used by that site's profile and proves endpoint rate-sum and finite-history energy identities. The explicit two-component cubic family has its exact accumulated midpoint error and componentwise bound. The defect composition proves a uniform componentwise O(h^2) bound. The shared D0.Analysis Taylor theorem derives its O(h^3) defect from C^3 regularity and an explicit uniform bound on the sampled interval; the geometry specialization composes it with the sampled-history result. The vector-valued Taylor/remainder composition now proves the same dimension-free constant in Euclidean norm. Its half-margin CAR application is transported through an isometric Euclidean lift and proved equal to the existing two-component finite recurrence. C^3 regularity at each point of the sampled interval, vector third-derivative and envelope bounds remain supplied hypotheses for the local API. The pointwise-margin corollary assumes global C^3 and pointwise strict chart inclusion, then uses compactness to derive the uniform derivative and envelope bounds and their positive uniform margin. The cubic-profile application bounds the Euclidean profile by the sum of its four coefficient norms on [0,1], derives the pointwise chart margin from that strict coefficient bound, and composes one eventual CAR threshold with the exact stencil source on the same recursive matter record. It returns the nonzero initial rate, but remains a finite-dimensional subset of the source's smooth matter family, not a reconstruction or selection of the original CAR preparation. The new uniform-mesh theorem derives an N0 threshold from the same delta-over-two estimate and proves the existing CAR complement positive for every N >= N0 with h=duration/N. Section 7.2 supplies the finite-step Eq. (24) error and states that fixed small normalized CAR slack survives for sufficiently fine h; the Lean result makes this eventual refinement claim explicit under the supplied analytic bounds. The actual CAR preparation and generator are not reconstructed. The exact signed cubic remainder is now lifted to the Euclidean vector of this same recursive record, with a dimension-free duration-times-third-derivative-coefficient-times-h-squared over 24 bound. A stronger cubic corollary returns this error bound together with CAR positivity and the exact five-point source at every site of every sufficiently fine uniform mesh. The original CAR construction, 40-to-3-to-1 substitution, all 16+24+2 Euler rows, and physical native Book/clock/source selection remain separate and open.

The quaternions `\mathbb H` are therefore the **maximal** associative division algebra over `\mathbb R`, and `Q_8` is exactly their unit group; the imaginary part `\mathrm{Im}(\mathbb H)=\mathrm{span}\{i,j,k\}` is `3`-

evidence_lines.heading: ### 01.19a.4 Conditional lattice and cut-and-project carrier route
evidence_lines.text: **Resolved (separation).** The question — is `K(9,11,13)` itself a `33D→3D` icosahedral cut-and-project with `A₅` symmetry on its rank-3 image? — is answered **no**, decidably (claim `D0-CARRIER-NOT-ICOSAHEDRAL-001`, Lean `D0.Claims.CarrierNotIcosahedral`, cert `vp_carrier_not_icosahedral.py`). `Aut(K(9,11,13)) = S₉×S₁₁×S₁₃`, and because the zone sizes are *distinct* (`9≠11≠13`) the induced symmetry on the three zone-classes — the entire symmetry the rank-3 physical image can inherit — is the **trivial** group (only the identity preserves the size assignment). The icosahedral group `A₅` has order `60`; it cannot embed into the trivial induced

evidence_lines.heading: ### 01.19a.4 Conditional lattice and cut-and-project carrier route
evidence_lines.text: **Third channel to the triple.** The `3D` physical slice (`A₅ = 2I/\{\pm1\} = \mathrm{PSL}(2,5) ⊂ SO(3)`) is a third independent route to `rank = 3`, alongside Frobenius (`ℍ` has three imaginary axes) and the linear-algebra theorem (the rank of a complete tripartite graph is its number of parts). These are three independent appearances of `3`; they do not prove that every admissible scene has exactly three zones.
